Make a pipeline that uses all the variables in the Ames dataset, and then fits Ridge Regression with all variables. 

Cross-validate this pipeline and compare the results to the ordinary linear regression.

Then fit the model on the whole dataset and get the coefficients. Make a plot of these coefficients compared to the ones from ordinary linear regression.

```{python}
import pandas as pd
import numpy as np
from sklearn.pipeline import Pipeline
from sklearn.compose import make_column_selector, ColumnTransformer
from sklearn.preprocessing import StandardScaler, OneHotEncoder, PolynomialFeatures
from sklearn.linear_model import LinearRegression, Ridge, Lasso, ElasticNet 
from sklearn.model_selection import train_test_split, cross_val_score
from sklearn.metrics import r2_score
```

Data cleaning: 
```{python}
# Read the data
ames = pd.read_csv("~/Desktop/GSB 544/Notes/Data/AmesHousing.csv", sep=",")

# Get rid of columns with mostly NaN values
good_cols = ames.isna().sum() < 100
ames = ames.loc[:,good_cols]

# Drop other NAs
ames = ames.dropna()
```

Setting up pipeline: 
```{python}
X = ames.drop(["SalePrice", "Order", "PID"], axis = 1) 
y = ames["SalePrice"]


ct = ColumnTransformer(
  [
    ("dummify", 
    OneHotEncoder(sparse_output = False, handle_unknown='ignore'), #you need the ignore so that something doesnt go wrong when you encounter new categories in your testing data that wasn't in your training data 
    make_column_selector(dtype_include=object)), #this dummifies anything that is an object s youdont have to name every single variable 
    ("standardize", 
    StandardScaler(), 
    make_column_selector(dtype_include=np.number))
  ],
  remainder = "passthrough"
)

lr_pipeline_1 = Pipeline(
  [("preprocessing", ct),
  ("linear_regression", LinearRegression())]
)
```


```{python}
cross_val_score(lr_pipeline_1, X, y, cv = 5, scoring = 'r2')
```

### Ridge lambda=0.001
```{python}
ridge_pipeline_0001 = Pipeline(
  [("preprocessing", ct),
  ("ridge alpha 0.001", Ridge(alpha=0.001))]
)
```

```{python}
scores1=cross_val_score(ridge_pipeline_0001, X, y, cv = 5, scoring = 'r2')
scores1.mean()
```

### Lasso
```{python}
lasso_pipeline_0001 = Pipeline(
  [("preprocessing", ct),
  ("ridge alpha 0.001", Lasso(alpha=0.001))]
)

lasso_pipeline_001 = Pipeline(
  [("preprocessing", ct),
  ("ridge alpha 0.01", Lasso(alpha=0.01))]
)

lasso_pipeline_01 = Pipeline(
  [("preprocessing", ct),
  ("ridge alpha 0.1", Lasso(alpha=0.1))]
)

lasso_pipeline_1 = Pipeline(
  [("preprocessing", ct),
  ("ridge alpha 1", Lasso(alpha=1))]
)

lasso_pipeline_10 = Pipeline(
  [("preprocessing", ct),
  ("ridge alpha 10", Lasso(alpha=10))]
)
```

```{python}
scores1lasso=cross_val_score(lasso_pipeline_0001, X, y, cv = 5, scoring = 'r2')
scores2lasso=cross_val_score(lasso_pipeline_001, X, y, cv = 5, scoring = 'r2')
scores3lasso=cross_val_score(lasso_pipeline_01, X, y, cv = 5, scoring = 'r2')
scores4lasso=cross_val_score(lasso_pipeline_1, X, y, cv = 5, scoring = 'r2')
scores5lasso=cross_val_score(lasso_pipeline_10, X, y, cv = 5, scoring = 'r2')

print(scores1lasso.mean(), scores2lasso.mean(), scores3lasso.mean(), scores4lasso.mean(), scores5lasso.mean())
```

Lambda=10 is the optimal choice for the Lasso regression from the options we ran. 


### Elastic Net
```{python}
elastic_pipeline_0001 = Pipeline(
  [("preprocessing", ct),
  ("ridge alpha 0.001", ElasticNet(alpha=0.001, l1_ratio=0.1))]
)

elastic_pipeline_001 = Pipeline(
  [("preprocessing", ct),
  ("ridge alpha 0.01", ElasticNet(alpha=0.01, l1_ratio=0.4))]
)

elastic_pipeline_01 = Pipeline(
  [("preprocessing", ct),
  ("ridge alpha 0.1", ElasticNet(alpha=0.1, l1_ratio=0.7))]
)

elastic_pipeline_1 = Pipeline(
  [("preprocessing", ct),
  ("ridge alpha 1", ElasticNet(alpha=1, l1_ratio=0.3))]
)

elastic_pipeline_10 = Pipeline(
  [("preprocessing", ct),
  ("ridge alpha 10", ElasticNet(alpha=10, l1_ratio=0.8))]
)
```

```{python}
scores1elastic=cross_val_score(elastic_pipeline_0001, X, y, cv = 5, scoring = 'r2')
scores2elastic=cross_val_score(elastic_pipeline_001, X, y, cv = 5, scoring = 'r2')
scores3elastic=cross_val_score(elastic_pipeline_01, X, y, cv = 5, scoring = 'r2')
scores4elastic=cross_val_score(elastic_pipeline_1, X, y, cv = 5, scoring = 'r2')
scores5elastic=cross_val_score(elastic_pipeline_10, X, y, cv = 5, scoring = 'r2')

print(scores1elastic.mean(), scores2elastic.mean(), scores3elastic.mean(), scores4elastic.mean(), scores5elastic.mean())
```

0.1 is the best lambda value with the tested ratios.
